intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Wolfram syndrome-2 (WFS2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CISD2 gene (611507) on chromosome 4q24.

checks.claim: Wolfram syndrome-2 (WFS2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CISD2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous mutation in a novel zinc-finger protein, ERIS, is responsible for Wolfram syndrome 2.
checks.explanation: The title says a homozygous mutation causes WFS2. CISD2 is the approved symbol for ZCD2.

checks.claim: The CISD2 gene is located on chromosome 4q24.
checks.evidence_quote: were mapped to the WFS2 locus at 4q22-25
checks.explanation: The abstract gives only the locus interval 4q22-25, not 4q24. A gene's chromosomal location counts as standard nomenclature, and 4q24 lies inside the stated interval.

paragraphs.text: El-Shanti et al. (2000) described Wolfram syndrome as an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder for which only insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and optic atrophy are necessary to make the diagnosis. In the families with the 4q-linked form (WFS2), El-Shanti et al. (2000) reported that diabetes insipidus was absent in all affected family members and that several patients had profound upper gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding. Mozzillo et al. (2014) listed sensorineural deafness as a feature of WFS2 and noted that WFS2 differs from WFS1 by the presence of bleeding upper intestinal ulcers and defective platelet aggregation.

checks.evidence_quote: is an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder for which only insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and optic atrophy are necessary to make the diagnosis

checks.claim: Only insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and optic atrophy are necessary to make the diagnosis of Wolfram syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: only insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and optic atrophy are necessary to make the diagnosis

checks.evidence_quote: There is an absence of diabetes insipidus in all affected family members.
checks.explanation: The abstract says diabetes insipidus was absent in all affected members of all 4 families, so it was also absent in the 3 families linked to 4q. Note that the paper does not present this as specific to the 4q-linked families.

checks.claim: In the families with the 4q-linked form of Wolfram syndrome (WFS2), several patients had profound upper gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding.
checks.evidence_quote: In addition, several patients have profound upper gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports ulceration in several of the 16 patients but does not say which families they came from. The abstract does not establish that they were in the 4q-linked families.

checks.evidence_quote: The clinical phenotype of WFS2 differs from WFS1 for the absence of diabetes insipidus and psychiatric disorders, and for the presence of bleeding upper intestinal ulcers and defective platelet aggregation.

paragraphs.text: El-Shanti et al. (2000) described Wolfram syndrome as an autosomal recessive disorder. Amr et al. (2007) found a homozygous mutation in patients with WFS2, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: El-Shanti et al. (2000) performed linkage analysis in 4 families with Wolfram syndrome. They significantly excluded linkage to the WFS1 region on chromosome 4p16 in 3 of the 4 families; the 2 affected individuals in the remaining family showed homozygosity for all 3 markers from the region of linkage on chromosome 4p16.1. In the other 3 families, El-Shanti et al. (2000) demonstrated linkage to chromosome 4q22-q24.

checks.claim: El-Shanti et al. (2000) performed linkage analysis in 4 families with Wolfram syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: we report the unique clinical findings and linkage-analysis results of 16 patients with Wolfram syndrome
checks.explanation: The abstract describes linkage analysis in the 4 families.

checks.claim: Linkage to the WFS1 region on chromosome 4p16 was significantly excluded in 3 of 4 Wolfram syndrome families studied by El-Shanti et al. (2000).
checks.evidence_quote: With the use of three microsatellite markers (D4S432, D4S3023, and D4S2366) reported to be linked to the chromosome 4p16.1 locus, we significantly excluded linkage in three of the four families.
checks.explanation: Stated directly. The 4p16.1 locus is the WFS1 region.

checks.claim: The 2 affected individuals in the remaining Wolfram syndrome family studied by El-Shanti et al. (2000) showed homozygosity for all 3 markers from the region of linkage on chromosome 4p16.1.
checks.evidence_quote: The two affected individuals in one family showed homozygosity for all three markers from the region of linkage on chromosome 4p16.1.

checks.claim: In the 3 Wolfram syndrome families in which 4p16 linkage was excluded, El-Shanti et al. (2000) demonstrated linkage to chromosome 4q22-q24.
checks.evidence_quote: For the other three families, genetic heterogeneity for Wolfram syndrome was verified by demonstration of linkage to chromosome 4q22-24.

paragraphs.text: El-Shanti et al. (2000) verified genetic heterogeneity for Wolfram syndrome by demonstrating linkage to chromosome 4q22-q24 in 3 families in which linkage to the WFS1 region on 4p16 had been excluded.

checks.claim: Wolfram syndrome is genetically heterogeneous, as shown by linkage to chromosome 4q22-q24 in 3 families in which linkage to the WFS1 region on 4p16 had been excluded.
checks.evidence_quote: For the other three families, genetic heterogeneity for Wolfram syndrome was verified by demonstration of linkage to chromosome 4q22-24.
checks.explanation: Stated directly, together with the exclusion of 4p16.1 linkage in those 3 families.

paragraphs.text: Amr et al. (2007) studied 3 consanguineous families of Jordanian descent with Wolfram syndrome that had been shown not to have mutations in the WFS1 gene and had been mapped to the WFS2 locus at 4q22-q25. They identified a homozygous mutation (E37Q) in the CISD2 gene (also called ZCD2), which encodes the protein ERIS (endoplasmic reticulum intermembrane small protein). The mutation predicted a single amino acid substitution, but it was also found to disrupt mRNA splicing by eliminating exon 2, resulting in the introduction of a premature stop codon.

paragraphs.text: Chen et al. (2009) found that Cisd2 deficiency in mice drove premature aging and caused mitochondrial breakdown and dysfunction, preceding nerve and muscle degeneration. They concluded that CISD2 is involved in mammalian life-span control. Cisd2 was primarily localized in the mitochondria, and mitochondrial degeneration appeared to have a direct phenotypic consequence that triggered the accelerated aging process in Cisd2 knockout mice.

checks.explanation: The abstract says mitochondrial breakdown and dysfunction come before nerve and muscle degeneration.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of 3 consanguineous families of Jordanian descent with WFS2, Amr et al. (2007) identified a homozygous 109G-C transversion in the CISD2 gene, predicting a glu37-to-gln (E37Q) substitution. The mutation caused aberrant splicing with elimination of exon 2, resulting in the introduction of a premature stop codon.

checks.explanation: The abstract places this mutation in the three Jordanian families, and the title says it is homozygous.
